era_note: Butte, Yuba and Sutter Counties, California, 2017-2022. The spec carries 131 forbidden_subjects and 27 forbidden_claims and all three Shorts stay inside the COURT RECORD, which is the safest ground this episode has. None of them says a dam failed, that anywhere was flooded or inundated, or that a wall of water was coming -- those are barred outright. None says anybody was given two hours or sixty minutes to leave; the sixty minutes in the record is the interval officials anticipated, not a grace period, and it is not quoted here at all. The number is always people ORDERED to leave, never people who evacuated, because the State's own expert testified nobody can enumerate the second thing -- that testimony is the subject of short293. Nothing here calls the decision precedent or settled law, says officials ignored warnings, says anyone recovered or was compensated, or names a Department of Water Resources employee. Dr. Cova is named because he is the department's RETAINED EXPERT, named in the published opinion, not an employee.
plate_pool_note: 118 approved plates at remotion/public/oroville/img. Each plate below was used by the finished film under the same narration: O088-O094 carry the expert's evidence, O095-O112 the no-defined-zone passage, O113-O118 ascertainability.

shorts.angle: The court did not find the evacuation zone was drawn too widely. It found no zone had ever been drawn.
shorts.avoids: Says nothing about a dam, water, or what was or was not coming. Does not say the case failed because the order turned out not to be mandatory -- that is the reported version and the spec bars it; the Short says that argument was made and is not what the court decided.
shorts.funnel_question_left_for_longform: If there was never a zone, what did the word mandatory mean that afternoon?
shorts.loop_join: The last line returns to the map the first line said everyone pictures.

lines.text: The obvious guess is that they lost because you cannot sue a state government. That is wrong. They could and they did.
source_lines: The obvious guess is that they lost because you cannot sue a state government. That is wrong. They could and they did. The case was filed, consolidated, heard, briefed and argued, and it went all the way to the Third District Court of Appeal.

lines.text: The Department of Water Resources argued that a mandatory evacuation had not really been binding. There is no penalty for staying.
source_lines: The Department of Water Resources argued in the lower court that a mandatory evacuation had not really been binding. There is no penalty for staying. Nobody comes to your house and carries you out. Some jurisdictions ordered, some recommended, and people made up their own minds.

lines.text: That was argued. It is on the record. And it is not what the court decided.
source_lines: That was argued. It is on the record. And it is not what the court decided.

lines.text: In fact, the evidence and briefing demonstrated there was no defined mandatory evacuation zone, and no defined group to which an order was issued.
source_lines: > In fact, the evidence and briefing submitted to the trial court demonstrated there was no defined mandatory evacuation zone and no defined group to which a mandatory evacuation order was issued.

lines.text: No defined zone. Not a zone that was drawn too widely, or drawn in the wrong place, or drawn and then lost. There was never a zone.
source_lines: No defined zone. Not a zone that was drawn too widely, or drawn in the wrong place, or drawn and then lost. There was never a zone.

lines.text: The orders did not describe a specific area, but rather such vague areas as: the low levels of Oroville and areas downstream.
source_lines: > They did not describe a specific area but rather such vague areas as: low levels of Oroville and areas downstream, the portion of Yuba County that is on the valley floor, and other communities along the Feather River.

lines.text: The instinctive picture of a mandatory evacuation is a map with a line on it, and a list of streets inside the line.
source_lines: The instinctive picture of a mandatory evacuation is a map with a line on it and a list of streets inside the line. That picture is what makes the word mandatory mean anything at all. And when the state and the plaintiffs between them put everything they had in front of a court, what the court found in the evidence was that no such line had ever been drawn.

source_lines: The instinctive picture of a mandatory evacuation is a map with a line on it and a list of streets inside the line. That picture is what makes the word mandatory mean anything at all. shorts.angle: A broadcast has no delivery receipt, so nobody -- including the people themselves -- could work out who was in the group.
shorts.avoids: The number is people ORDERED to leave, never people who evacuated, which is the distinction the expert's testimony turns on and which the spec bars getting wrong. Names Dr. Cova because the published opinion does, as the department's retained expert; no employee is named.
shorts.funnel_question_left_for_longform: She had the receipts from her own two days and still could not say if she was in it. Why?
shorts.loop_join: The last line hands the first line's question back unanswered.

lines.text: The department retained an expert on human population evacuations due to natural disasters.
source_lines: The department retained an expert. His name was Doctor Cova and the opinion describes him as an expert on human population evacuations due to natural disasters.

lines.text: He stated there is no known method to enumerate who evacuated and who did not, in a given area and time frame, in response to a broadcast evacuation order.
source_lines: > Dr. Cova stated there is no known method to enumerate who evacuated and who did not in a given area and time frame in response to a broadcasted evacuation order.

lines.text: Read that as engineering rather than law. A broadcast is a signal sent to nobody in particular. It has no delivery receipt.
source_lines: Read that as a piece of engineering rather than as a piece of law. A broadcast is a signal sent to nobody in particular. It has no delivery receipt. It does not know who heard it, and it cannot know who acted on it, and there is no instrument anywhere that can reconstruct that afterwards.

lines.text: This lack of ascertainability would also prevent individual class members from self-identifying as meeting the class definition.
source_lines: > This lack of ascertainability would also prevent individual class members from self-identifying as meeting the class definition.

lines.text: Ascertainability. Whether the people in a group can be worked out at all.
source_lines: Ascertainability. Whether the people in a group can be worked out at all.

lines.text: A woman holding the receipts from her own two days, reading the definition of the class she was trying to represent, could not have told you with certainty whether she was in it.
source_lines: And the second half of that sentence is the part that should stop a viewer, because it is not about lawyers. It says the members could not identify themselves. Denise Johnson, holding the receipts from her own two days, reading the definition of the class she was trying to represent, could not have told you with certainty whether she was in it.

lines.text: Nobody could. Not the state, not the court, and not the hundred and eighty-eight thousand.
source_lines: Nobody could. Not the state, not the court, and not the hundred and eighty-eight thousand.

shorts.angle: Four people asked the State to reimburse two days of expenses, and were ordered to pay the State's costs of the appeal.
shorts.avoids: Says nobody recovered, settled or was compensated -- the spec bars claiming they did, and the record is the opposite. Does not call the decision precedent or binding on anyone else.
shorts.funnel_question_left_for_longform: Two days of expenses went in. A costs order came out. What happened in between?
shorts.loop_join: The last line puts the bill back beside the claim the first line made.

lines.text: Four people put their names on a complaint on behalf of everybody who had been ordered out, asking for the out-of-pocket cost of the two days.
source_lines: And four people — Francis Bechtel, Jacob Klein, Chantel Ramirez and Denise Johnson — put their names on a complaint against the California Department of Water Resources, on behalf of everybody who had been ordered out, asking for the out-of-pocket cost of the two days and the loss of use of their homes for the two days.

lines.text: That is the entire claim. Not the dam. Not the crisis. Not damages for fear. Expenses, for two days.
source_lines: That is the entire claim. Not the dam. Not the crisis. Not damages for fear. Expenses, for two days.

lines.text: A class action is for a harm small enough that no single person could sensibly litigate it, spread across enough people that it adds up to something real.
source_lines: A class action is a device for a particular kind of problem: a harm small enough that no single person could sensibly litigate it, spread across enough people that it adds up to something real. Two nights out of a rented house is exactly that harm. No lawyer takes that case for one person. For a hundred and eighty-eight thousand, it becomes a case.

lines.text: But the price of using it is that the group has to be a group. A court has to be able to say, of any person, whether they are in it or out of it.
source_lines: But the price of using it is that the group has to be a group. A court has to be able to say, of any person in California, whether they are in it or out of it — because a judgment binds everybody inside the definition, including people who never heard of the case.

lines.text: Class certification was denied. On the fifteenth of March, twenty twenty-two, the Third District Court of Appeal affirmed.
source_lines: Class certification was denied. It was denied to the Bechtel plaintiffs, and it was denied in the same ninety-page ruling to a second group of Oroville property owners, who did not appeal.
On the fifteenth of March, twenty twenty-two, the Third District Court of Appeal affirmed.

lines.text: The disposition of an appeal is usually two sentences of housekeeping. Here they are.
source_lines: The disposition of an appeal is usually two sentences of housekeeping. Here they are.

lines.text: The judgment is affirmed. Respondent Department of Water Resources shall recover its costs on appeal.
source_lines: > The judgment is affirmed. Respondent Department of Water Resources shall recover its costs on appeal.

lines.text: The four people who had asked the State to reimburse two days of expenses were ordered to pay the State's costs of the appeal.
source_lines: In ordinary English: the four people who had asked the State to reimburse two days of expenses were ordered to pay the State's costs of the appeal in which it had established that no one could be shown to have been ordered to leave.
